Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between IPMN and ND samples, provide a summary of enriched pathways in IPMN compared to ND.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The dataset (Wang_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS2A.csv) reports proteomic log₂–fold changes and FDRs for 9,417 proteins comparing 64 IPMNs to 76 grossly normal pancreatic ducts (ND). Key observations include highly significant upregulation of mucins (MUC5AC, MUC13), trefoil factors (TFF1–3), REG4, and down-regulation of classic secretory enzymes (e.g., PRSS1/2) and ribosomal proteins.  

Keywords  
• Mucin secretion  
• Translation machinery  
• Immune response  
• ECM remodeling  
• Protein export  

Candidate Genes  
• MUC5AC, MUC13  
• TFF1, TFF2, TFF3  
• REG4  
• RPLP1 (ribosomal)  
• C1R (complement)

Analysis  
IPMNs exhibit strong suppression of translational and secretory machinery—evidenced by down-regulation of ribosome, peptide biosynthesis, SRP-mediated targeting, and pancreatic secretion pathways—reflecting a reprogramming away from normal exocrine function. Concurrently, immune and remodeling programs are activated: KEGG/Reactome show enrichment of phagosome, Salmonella-infection, and TP53 regulatory pathways, while MSigDB Hallmarks highlight interferon-γ response, complement activation, and EMT. GO terms for actin organization and endosomal transport further support increased cell motility and immune trafficking. The high up/down ratio in Hallmark gene sets (5.0) underscores dominant inflammatory and stromal-remodeling signals in IPMN versus ND.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate suppression of translation at the protein level (e.g., polysome profiling).  
2. Assess immune infiltration (e.g., single-cell/IF staining for macrophage markers) to link phagosome signatures to cell types.  
3. Measure mucin secretion and trefoil factor levels in cyst fluid to correlate proteomic changes with biomarker potential.  
4. Explore mTORC1/mTORC2 activity given ORA-identified mTORC1 signaling enrichment.
